correctness.rationale: Frozen RESULT.md blob 422445f5aadf6a21f7a134746c2c1fabe1a19788 uses the exact Pham PNE1 vector field (x'=y, y'=−x+yz, z'=−x−axy−bxz+c). Direct differentiation E=(x²+y²)/2 gives E'=y²z. Generator invariance on compact support forces ∫y²z=0. If its positive and negative weighted parts both vanish, y²|z|=0 continuously on invariant support. If z is nonzero on any interval then y=0 there, hence x=0 and uniqueness extends x=y=0, while z'=c produces an unbounded complete orbit, impossible. Otherwise z≡0, x,y execute a harmonic circle but z'=0 imposes x(1+ay)=c for all time; its nonzero constant −c Fourier coefficient makes this impossible for c≠0. Therefore both weighted half-space integrals are equal and strictly positive for every compactly supported invariant μ. Every nonempty compact invariant set carries a time-average invariant measure, so it meets both z signs; periodic continuity forces plane crossings. Recomputed E' exactly and checked the harmonic constraint, not the numerical chaos evidence. At c=0 an equilibrium line defeats strictness; no recurrence existence is asserted.
